findings.description: The diff makes `.run/context-class` a behavior-governing input: every skill's generated context_discipline block (auditing-security, implementing-tasks, reviewing-code) and ride.md instruct the agent to read it and apply thresholds based on its value. The script that writes it, `session-start/loa-context-class.sh`, is not part of the diff, is listed in the README Hook Registry but not in the README 'Active (registered in settings.hooks.json)' table, and `settings.hooks.json` is not updated in the diff. No consumer constrains the value to the two expected tokens (`long` / `standard`).
findings.failure_mode: If the hook is not actually registered, is blocked by hook-guard, or the file is stale, hand-edited, or committed into a target repo where `.run/` is not ignored, the agent reads arbitrary file content as trusted configuration. Unexpected content yields undefined threshold behavior at best and, if read verbatim into context, a small prompt-injection surface at worst.
findings.suggested_fix: Have `loa-context-class.sh` write only the literal token `long` or `standard`. Make consumers (skills, `/loa` display, workflow-state.sh) accept only those two tokens and fall back to `long` on anything else, rather than echoing the file into context. Confirm `.run/` is gitignored in mounted repos. Add the hook to the README active-files table and to `settings.hooks.json` so documentation matches registration.
